beliefs: The first character is shifted backward by 2 in the alphabet (a->y, b->z, ..., z->x; A->Y, ..., Z->X) [E7, E8, E9, E10]
All characters after the first are left unchanged, including letters, digits, spaces, and symbols [E1, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8]
If the first character is not a letter (digit, space, symbol, control char, emoji), it is left unchanged [E1, E11, E12]
Non-ASCII letters are shifted backward by 2 in Unicode code point order, wrapping within the contiguous letter block (é->ç, É->Ç, ü->ú, ß->Ý, ñ->ï, à->Þ, ø->ö, æ->ä, œ->ő) [E11, E12]
The shift for non-ASCII letters uses code-point arithmetic within the contiguous run of same-case letters containing the character, not alphabet position [E12]
notes: E12 shows non-ASCII letters shift by -2 in code point order (à->Þ, ø->ö, œ->ő), not by alphabet position; the earlier 'case block' scan was wrong because it scanned by code point but I mislabeled it. Now using code-point -2 within the contiguous same-case letter run.
